report.source_text: At the time of discharge, the patient had returned to full orientation, with resolution of confusion and marked improvement in cognitive and motor functions. He was able to walk unassisted, follow commands, and perform activities of daily living independently. Mild residual fatigue and occasional mood fluctuations were reported but did not interfere with his functional status.

clinician.final_diagnosis: ADEM (Acute Disseminated Encephalomyelitis), most likely triggered by a recent viral illness
clinician.trajectory_summary: One week prior to admission, the patient developed a viral prodrome characterized by arthralgias, myalgias, and severe headache, initially misdiagnosed as complex migraine with nonspecific MRI at an outside hospital. He subsequently presented with acute encephalopathy (GCS 10/15), confusion, and meningeal irritation signs. Workup revealed CSF lymphocytic pleocytosis with elevated protein and negative infectious studies (HSV PCR, bacterial cultures), and brain MRI demonstrated new multifocal T2/FLAIR hyperintensities in the left hemisphere, right parietal and temporal lobes with mild leptomeningeal enhancement, consistent with acute demyelination. He received high-dose intravenous methylprednisolone with significant clinical improvement over 3 days, and was discharged with full orientation and functional recovery.
